hypothesis: Failure analysis shows pitches are systematically misread (D-G-E-A instead of C4-C5-C4-C5; stepwise scale instead of arpeggio in D-major). This is a vision-grounding problem, not a prompt-knowledge problem — the model knows the rules but can't read note positions on the staff. Current preproc applies aggressive enhancement (autocontrast+unsharp+sharpness 2x) at 300dpi after a custom crop that may misalign staff context. Try the simplest higher-fidelity input: render at 400dpi, drop the destructive sharpness/unsharp chain, and skip the custom crop (PyMuPDF's full page is fine and preserves margins/staff context). One change with a clear ablation: swap _render_page_cropped + _enhance with a clean 400dpi full-page render. If pitches improve here, that confirms the enhancement pipeline was harming vision more than helping.
lesson: Dropping the destructive enhancement chain (autocontrast + UnsharpMask radius=2/percent=200 + Sharpness 2x) and the luminance-threshold staff crop, while bumping render DPI from 300 to 400, lifted overall score 0.0→0.222 and made the c-major scale fixture solvable for the first time. This confirms the prior preproc was net-harmful for Gemini 3 Pro Vision on engraved staff notation: aggressive sharpening likely introduced ringing artifacts around stems/noteheads/staff lines that degraded position grounding, and the bbox-tight crop was stripping margin context the model uses to anchor staff position. However, only the simplest fixture flipped — octave leap, both rhythm fixtures, 3/4 meter, and D-major key signature all still score 0.0, so the residual failures are NOT a preproc problem. They split into at least two classes: (a) pitch/octave localization on wider intervals (octave leap, D-major arpeggio) which a clean full-page render at 400dpi did not fix, suggesting either DPI is still insufficient for fine vertical notehead disambiguation OR the model needs explicit staff-line reference scaffolding in the prompt; and (b) rhythm/meter reading (quarter-eighth, dotted-quarter, 3/4) which is orthogonal to vision quality and points at prompt/decoding rather than image fidelity. Preproc has likely now hit diminishing returns as a single-knob lever.
proposed_next: Split the remaining error space: try a higher DPI (600) to see if pitch-localization fixtures (octave leap, D-major) move, and independently try a prompt-level intervention for rhythm/meter (e.g., explicit time-signature + beam-counting checklist or chain-of-thought) since those failures are unlikely to be vision-bound.

hypothesis: Iter 1's preproc bump moved the score but pitches are still systematically misread (D-G-E-A vs C4-C5-C4-C5) and rhythm/meter/key fixtures are stuck at zero — these failures look prompt-bound, not vision-bound. Building on the open hypothesis from iter 1, I'll do a structurally large prompt rewrite: replace the current single-shot prompt with an explicit, staged instruction that (a) reads and echoes the clef + key signature + time signature first, (b) names every note head with its staff-line position before assigning pitch, (c) counts beams/flags/dots per note and verifies each measure sums to the time signature, and (d) emits MusicXML only after these checks. A bigger rewrite is warranted because the noise floor isn't yet measurable (only 2 iters) and small prompt tweaks would likely be lost in noise.
lesson: A structurally large prompt rewrite to a multi-stage 'echo CLEF/KEY/TIME, then enumerate staff positions, then count beams/dots, then emit MusicXML' protocol regressed the score from 0.222 to 0.0 across all six fixtures, including the C-major-scale fixture that the prior prompt got right. The actor's manual probe showed the staged prompt CAN produce correct output, so this is not a 'prompt is logically wrong' failure — it's that long chain-of-thought-style protocols on Gemini 3 Pro Vision appear to bias the model toward emitting 'plausible-looking' completions (generic scales, default keys) rather than grounded staff reads, and they inflate response length enough to hit 504 DEADLINE_EXCEEDED (the actor had to bump timeout 120s→300s). The lesson for the prompt axis: on this model, terse spec-style prompts like iter-1's outperform staged self-verification protocols, likely because the long preamble dilutes attention on the image and the 'verify each measure sums to time signature' step encourages the model to fabricate measures that satisfy the check rather than report what it sees. Also note that with N=1 and only 6 fixtures, a single bad sample on the easy C-major fixture wipes ~0.11 of score — run-to-run variance at N=1 is large enough that 'big rewrite' prompt experiments need N≥3 before drawing conclusions.
proposed_next: Revert prompt structure toward the iter-1 terse style but keep the prompts.py/transcribe.py file split, then add N=3 self-consistency voting on <pitch> per measure to suppress the variance that just bit us.

proposed_next: Per-measure cropping with a focused single-measure prompt — give the model one measure at a time at high DPI so octave leaps and rhythmic flags get full visual attention, since whole-page transcription is where the systematic perception bias lives.

hypothesis: The two high-confidence wins are both preproc (iter-1 DPI bump +0.222, iter-4 per-measure cropping +0.111), and the three stuck-at-zero fixtures (octave-leap, dotted-quarter, D-major key) are all vision-grounding failures where the model can't reliably localize notehead position on the staff or count flags. lesson: Adding a left-gutter pitch ruler with labeled staff lines (F5/D5/B4/G4/E4) and faint colored guide lines extending across the staff produced a zero net delta but a revealing per-fixture pattern: D-major-2-sharps improved (0→0.5) while C-major-scale regressed (1.0→0.5). The structural lesson: vision-grounding overlays can simultaneously fix one failure mode and introduce another when they touch the music region itself, so future overlay work must keep annotations strictly OUT of the staff (gutter-only labels, no cross-staff tinted lines) or use post-hoc text anchors rather than rendered guides. Also notable: this is the second preproc iter where 'add more information to the image' produced no net delta or regression (iter-2 prompt rewrite, this iter), suggesting the easy preproc wins (DPI, per-measure cropping) are exhausted and additive overlays now hit a tradeoff frontier rather than a free improvement.

hypothesis: Both high-confidence wins are preproc (DPI bump +0.222, per-measure cropping +0.111), and the four stuck fixtures (octave-leap, both rhythm, D-major) are vision-bound — the model can't ground notehead Y-position or count beam-flags reliably. This builds on the per-measure crop pipeline already in place and directly attacks octave-leap and D-major key, which are pure pitch-localization failures.
lesson: Extending the iter-5 pitch ruler with bilateral (left+right) gutters, explicit ledger-line tick marks at A5/C6/C4/A3, and a fix to staff_left detection that excludes left-of-staff part-name text produced a real +0.111 gain — unsticking octave-leap (0→1.0) and dotted-quarter (0→1.0), plus 3/4-time (0.5→1.0). The key insight is that iter-5's ruler was directionally correct but underpowered: a single-sided gutter with only one ledger position above/below is insufficient when noteheads sit far from the labeled column or extend ≥2 ledger lines off the staff (octave-leap C4 needs the C4 tick; dotted-quarter spans C4-D4 territory). The bilateral labels eliminate horizontal-distance estimation error, and the explicit tick-marks for ledger positions give the model a calibrated anchor for off-staff pitches rather than asking it to extrapolate. Equally important: iter-5's regression was likely caused in part by the 'Music' part-name text leaking into crops and competing for visual attention — fixing staff_left to anchor to actual staff-line columns removed that distractor. This contradicts iter-5's reflector framing that the ruler concept itself was unhelpful; the concept was right, the implementation was incomplete. D-major-2-sharps and quarter-eighth remain stuck at 0, suggesting key-signature reading and rhythm/duration discrimination are NOT pitch-localization failures and won't be fixed by ruler enhancements — they need a different angle (key-signature annotation, beam/flag highlighting, or duration-grid overlay).
proposed_next: Add a key-signature annotation pass: detect sharps/flats at the start of each crop and render an explicit text label (e.g. 'Key: D major (F#, C#)') in the top gutter so the model doesn't have to count accidentals.

hypothesis: Both high-confidence wins are preproc (DPI bump +0.222, per-measure cropping +0.111), and the four stuck fixtures (octave-leap pitch, both rhythm, D-major key) are vision-bound: the model can't ground notehead position against the staff or count beam stems reliably. The most promising untried open hypothesis is the staff-line reference annotation (iter-4 open) combined with a key-signature label gutter (iter-6 open) — both directly attack the grounding problem on stuck fixtures without changing the proven crop+vote pipeline. I'll add an annotation pass to each per-measure crop: a labeled E-G-B-D-F side ruler in the left gutter and an explicit 'Key: <name> (<accidentals>)' text label in the top gutter, so the model has a visible coordinate system and doesn't need to count sharps. This is a structurally larger preproc experiment (delta should clear the 0.117 noise floor) and stacks on the two confirmed preproc wins.
lesson: Adding a tall TOP gutter with key-signature text and a sharp/flat cheat-sheet to every per-measure crop regressed the score from 0.556 to 0.333 even though the heuristic detector itself was correct on all 6 fixtures (D-major correctly flagged as 2 sharps, others as natural). The regressions hit dotted-quarter (1/1→0/1) and 3/4 (2/2→1/2) — fixtures that had nothing to do with key signature — while the targeted D-major fixture stayed at 0/2. This suggests that crop aspect ratio and on-image textual content are themselves load-bearing inputs to the VLM: a 360px top gutter changes the staff's relative vertical position and forces the model to allocate attention to dense letter-shaped tokens (KEY SIGNATURE, F#-C#-G#…, Bb-Eb-Ab…) that compete with notehead/stem reading. The lesson generalizes beyond this iter: stacking annotation gutters is NOT free — each gutter shrinks the staff's share of the image and adds OCR-able distractors, and the cost can exceed the benefit even when the annotation is factually correct. Iter-5's left+right pitch ruler was tolerable because it sat beside the staff at the staff's own height; a top gutter is a different beast because it competes vertically. Pure-text annotation (cheat sheets, key names) appears to be especially harmful — likely because the VLM tries to read it as music-adjacent context. Future preproc experiments should prefer overlays that sit on/beside the staff at staff height and avoid adding rendered prose; if key-signature info must be conveyed, try the prompt channel or a minimal symbolic mark (e.g., circling the actual sharps already on the staff) rather than a text panel.
proposed_next: Move key-signature hinting from an on-image text gutter into the prompt text only (pass detected key as a string in the message), keeping the iter-5 left/right pitch ruler unchanged, to isolate whether textual annotation in-image is the regression driver.

hypothesis: Both high-confidence wins are preproc (DPI bump +0.222, per-measure cropping +0.111) and the four stuck fixtures (octave-leap, both rhythm, D-major key) are vision-bound where notehead-on-staff-line localization and beam/flag counting matter. Iter-7's text-gutter annotation regressed (-0.222), suggesting in-image text confuses the model. The cleanest open hypothesis from iter-4 is structural staff-line reference marks (no text labels crossing the staff) — annotate each measure crop with a thin side ruler showing E-G-B-D-F line positions in the gutter only, giving the model a coordinate system for pitch grounding without polluting the music area. This addresses octave-leap and D-major directly while keeping the per-measure crop + N=3 voting that already work.
lesson: In-image annotations have a non-monotonic relationship with score: iter-6's colored guide lines THROUGH the music area (+0.111) and iter-7's text-heavy top gutter (-0.222) and iter-8's clean side-only ticks (-0.111 vs iter-6) together show that the model uses guide lines drawn across the staff as an active pitch-tracking aid, not just a passive coordinate frame. Stripping the in-music guide lines — even while keeping correct gutter ticks — caused octave-leap and 3/4-meter to collapse from passing to 0.0, which means the lines were doing real localization work for noteheads sitting on/between specific staff lines. The 'text in image confuses the model' hypothesis from iter-7 was probably correct about the text labels, but it conflated text with the colored lines themselves; the lines and the text were two separate variables and only the text needed to go. Future preproc work should keep the in-music guide lines from iter-6 and only iterate on what's drawn in the gutters, treating the music-area overlay and the gutter overlay as independent levers.
proposed_next: Restore iter-6's in-music colored guide lines while keeping iter-8's text-free single-letter side ticks, isolating the 'text-free' improvement from the 'no in-music lines' regression.

hypothesis: The two stuck failure modes are octave-leap pitch and rhythmic flag/beam counting — both vision-bound but tractable via structured chain-of-thought. Preproc has plateaued (6 attempts, avg +0.019, last 3 iters all regressed or got reverted), and category stats show prompt has higher avg_delta (+0.056) with fewer attempts. The decisive move is a structurally larger prompt experiment: a per-measure two-stage prompt that first asks Gemini to enumerate visible noteheads with staff-line position (line/space + which line) and beam/flag count as explicit observations, THEN derive pitch+duration from those observations. This forces the model to ground perception before transcription, which is exactly where octave-leap and rhythm fail. Keep N=3 voting and the iter-6 preproc baseline so the delta is attributable to the prompt change.
lesson: Forcing a structured two-stage chain-of-thought (enumerate noteheads with staff-position/beam/flag/dot observations, then derive MusicXML) did NOT move the aggregate score (0.222→0.222) but it shuffled which fixtures pass: 04-key D-major went 0.0→0.5 while 02-rhythm/01-quarter-eighth and 02-rhythm/02-dotted-quarter both regressed 1.0→0.0. This is informative — the explicit observation pass apparently helps the model commit to a key signature it would otherwise ignore, but the verbose flag/beam enumeration actively HURTS rhythm fixtures that were already passing under the simpler iter-8 prompt, suggesting the model second-guesses correct rhythm reads when forced to verbalize beam counts. Output tokens grew ~45% with no net gain, so longer structured CoT is not free and not monotonically better. The pattern across iters 2, 7, 8, 9 is now clear: any prompt or preproc change that adds a new layer of structured guidance trades wins on one fixture for losses on another, leaving aggregate near 0.222 — the failure modes are not all the same shape, and a single prompt scaffold cannot grip all of them simultaneously. Octave-leap (01-pitch/02) remained at 0.0 even with explicit staff-position enumeration, which is strong evidence the side-ruler+CoT combination still does not solve octave disambiguation — the model's vision pass is the bottleneck, not its reasoning scaffold.
proposed_next: Try fixture-conditional or per-failure-mode prompting (e.g., a separate rhythm-only verification pass that ONLY counts beams/flags and is merged into the Stage-B output), or revisit N>3 self-consistency voting with disagreement-triggered re-asks, since uniform prompt scaffolds keep trading wins for losses.

hypothesis: The two high-confidence wins are both preproc (DPI bump, per-measure cropping at 600 DPI with N=3 voting), and we've now plateaued at 0.556 best with four stuck fixtures all sharing the same root cause: the model can't ground notehead Y-position to staff lines (octave-leap, D-major key) or count beam/flag stems (both rhythm fixtures). Iter-9's reverted prompt rewrite was the right idea but too uniform; iter-9's open hypothesis explicitly calls for a per-failure-mode verification pass. I propose a structurally larger experiment: a two-stage chain inside the existing per-measure cropping pipeline — Stage A produces the candidate measure transcription as today, Stage B is a dedicated verification pass that takes (crop + Stage-A output) and is asked ONLY to verify pitch octave AND beam/flag count against the image, returning corrections. This addresses both stuck failure modes in one shot and is large enough to clear the 0.111 noise floor.
lesson: A two-call Stage-A/Stage-B verification chain at the same crop+resolution does NOT break the 0.556 plateau: the verifier inherits the transcriber's vision failure modes because both calls see the same pixels at the same scale, so a second look cannot recover information the first look couldn't extract. The four stuck fixtures (octave-leap, dotted-quarter, partial 3/4, partial D-major) are bounded by Gemini's spatial grounding on the supplied crop — not by reasoning depth or prompt structure — which means iterating on prompt scaffolding (iter-9 heavy observation list, iter-10 verifier pass) recovers the plateau but cannot exceed it. The score recovery from iter-9's 0.222 to 0.556 also confirms iter-9's lesson that dense in-prompt observation lists actively hurt accuracy; a lean Stage-A prompt is the right baseline. Future progress on these fixtures almost certainly requires changing what the model sees (different crop geometry, higher DPI, targeted overlays per failure mode, or notehead-localized sub-crops), not how it is asked to reason about it.
proposed_next: Give Stage B a DIFFERENT view than Stage A — e.g. a per-notehead zoomed sub-crop with a staff-line ruler overlay — so the verifier sees pixels Stage A didn't.

hypothesis: The plateau at 0.556 is vision-bound: same four fixtures (octave-leap pitch, both rhythm, D-major key) keep failing because the model can't ground noteheads to staff lines or count beams reliably. Both high-confidence wins were preproc (DPI bump, per-measure cropping), and iter-10's lesson is explicit — a Stage-B verifier on the same pixels can't recover info Stage-A missed; we need a structurally different view. Combine open hypotheses from iters 4 and 6: annotate each per-measure crop with (a) a labeled left-side staff-line ruler (E-G-B-D-F + ledger lines above/below) so noteheads have an explicit Y-coordinate system, AND (b) a top-gutter text label naming the detected key signature (e.g. 'Key: D major (F#, C#)') so the model doesn't recount accidentals per measure. This directly attacks both stuck failure modes (pitch grounding + key) with a structurally bigger preproc change than anything since iter 4, large enough to clear the 0.120 sigma.
lesson: Combining a labeled left-side staff-line ruler (with octave numbers like E4/G4/B4) AND a top-gutter key-signature caption produced exactly zero movement (0.5556 → 0.5556) — same four fixtures stuck. This is the fifth preproc overlay attempt (iters 5, 6, 7, 8, 11) and the pattern is now clear: structural overlays drawn into the image margins do not unlock the stuck fixtures. Iter-6's small win came from minimal tick marks; iter-7 (text-heavy) regressed; iter-8 (single-letter side rulers) regressed; iter-11 (octave-numbered ruler + key caption) was a no-op. The model either (a) ignores gutter annotations entirely when they're decorative, or (b) the stuck failures (octave-leap pitch, dotted-quarter rhythm, both meter/key half-credit) are not pitch-grounding failures at all — they're symbolic/counting failures (beam counting, dot detection, accidental-to-key inference) that no amount of coordinate scaffolding in the margins can fix. The plateau at 0.5556 has now survived 6 consecutive iters; preproc-overlay is a saturated lever.
proposed_next: Abandon in-image overlays entirely; try a two-pass pipeline where pass 1 extracts structured primitives (notehead Y-positions, beam counts, dot presence) via targeted per-element crops, and pass 2 assembles them — moving the hard work out of one-shot vision into discrete sub-questions.

hypothesis: Plateau at 0.556 is vision-bound on the same four fixtures, and iter 10 proved that a second pass at the same crop+resolution cannot break it — the verifier inherits the transcriber's failure modes. Implement iter 11's open hypothesis: a two-pass primitive-extraction pipeline. Pass 1 generates per-notehead micro-crops (~200x200px around each detected notehead) with a staff-line ruler overlay drawn from detected staff geometry, asking Gemini ONE question per crop (which staff position? how many beams/flags? dotted?). Pass 2 assembles the structured primitives into MusicXML deterministically. This decomposes the hard vision problem into discrete sub-questions where each call sees pixels the prior pipeline never showed it — addressing the root cause (notehead Y-grounding, beam counting) rather than retrying the same view.
lesson: The two-pass primitive-extraction pipeline (per-notehead micro-crops + deterministic MusicXML assembly) collapsed the score from 0.556 to 0.111, losing even previously-passing fixtures like the C-major scale and 3/4 time. The failure mode is informative: decomposing the vision task into per-notehead sub-questions trades one hard problem (read the whole staff) for many coupled hard problems (detect every notehead, ground each Y-position against staff lines, count flags/beams, then reassemble durations into measures that sum to the time signature). Each sub-stage has its own error rate, and errors compound multiplicatively — a single missed or duplicate notehead detection corrupts the entire measure's rhythm, and the deterministic assembler has no way to recover because it trusts the primitive list. The dotted-quarter fixture surviving is a tell: it's the one case where the measure has so few notes that primitive-detection noise can't accumulate. This contradicts the iter-11 hypothesis premise that 'the verifier inherits the transcriber's failure modes' — actually, the holistic single-pass transcriber was using global staff context (clef, key sig, neighboring notes, beat structure) to constrain its guesses, and stripping that context out hurt more than the per-notehead zoom helped. Lesson: for this model on this task, holistic prompting beats decomposition, because Gemini's musical priors are doing more work than the pixel-level vision, and a 200x200 crop of one notehead removes the very cues (relative position, beam-grouping, beat alignment) the model relies on.
proposed_next: Revert to the iter-10 single-pass pipeline as baseline, then try targeted augmentations that ADD context rather than replace it — e.g., overlay a staff-line ruler annotation on the full-measure crop so the model sees explicit Y-grounding without losing the holistic view.

The two high-confidence wins are both preproc (DPI bump + per-measure 600 DPI cropping with N=3 voting), so the right move is to restore that exact iter-10 configuration as the baseline and then layer ONE additive change: overlay an explicit staff-line ruler annotation (E-G-B-D-F labels in the side gutter) on each per-measure crop, addressing the four stuck fixtures' root cause (notehead Y-grounding for octave-leap pitch and D-major key). This combines open hypotheses from iters 4 and 12 — additive context that doesn't replace the holistic view — and is structurally larger than the failed in-music overlays from iters 5–7 because it lives entirely in the side gutter and ticks each staff line individually. If the score returns to ≥0.556, we know iter-10 baseline is recoverable and the ruler is the next probe; if it clears 0.667, we've cracked one stuck pitch fixture.

The structurally larger refactors of iters 11–12 (multi-pass primitive extraction + deterministic assembly) regressed hard (0.111–0.333), suggesting that decomposing the task into separate notehead-detection + answer-aggregation passes loses more than it gains at this scale — the holistic single-prompt view with the side-gutter ruler is genuinely the local maximum, and the next gains must come from a *different axis* (prompt content, verification logic, or a targeted second-pass on detected ambiguities) rather than re-architecting the pipeline. Notably, the planner's hypothesis that adding a side-gutter ruler would clear a stuck fixture was already realized in iter-10 — iter-13's actor correctly reinterpreted the goal as 'restore iter-10' rather than 'add a ruler on top of iter-10', because the ruler was already part of the iter-10 baseline.
proposed_next: Add a targeted Stage-C verifier that re-prompts ONLY for the four stuck-fixture failure modes (dotted-rhythm presence, key-signature sharp count, time-signature numerator, octave number on leaps) using the existing per-measure crops, and merge its answers into the holistic output rather than replacing them.

hypothesis: The 0.556 plateau is vision-bound on four fixtures (octave-leap pitch, both rhythm, D-major key) and iter-10 proved a second pass at the same crop+resolution can't break it because the verifier inherits the transcriber's failure modes. The fix is to give the verifier DIFFERENT pixels: extract per-notehead zoom crops (with a staff-line ruler overlay for Y-grounding) and per-stem zoom crops (for beam/flag counting), ask Gemini targeted sub-questions on each (octave number, beam count, dot presence, sharp count), then merge those answers into the existing per-measure holistic output as a Stage-C corrector. This combines the iter-11 'discrete sub-questions' open hypothesis with iter-10's 'different view for verifier' open hypothesis, attacks all four stuck fixtures at once, and preserves the iter-10/13 baseline (so we can only gain). Big enough delta to clear the 0.158 sigma if even two stuck fixtures unstick.
lesson: Stage-C per-notehead zoom crops are a double-edged sword: narrowing the view to ~3x notehead width DOES unstick pitch fixtures (octave-leap went 0→1.0, c-major-scale stayed 1.0) because Y-position against the side ruler is unambiguous in a tight crop, but the SAME narrow crop DESTROYS rhythm reading because beam/flag identity is a horizontal-context feature — a quarter note and a single eighth look identical when you crop away the neighboring note that the beam connects to. Net zero is therefore a structural finding, not noise: zoom helps vertical (pitch) sub-questions and hurts horizontal (rhythm) sub-questions, so a uniform 'one zoom per notehead' policy can't win. The corrector merge logic also inherits the transcriber's measure boundaries, so any over/under-detection of noteheads (the right-align trim is a band-aid for clef/time/key false positives in measure 1) silently shifts which Stage-B note gets corrected.
